codexV4Verdict.standing: REJECT - blockers V4-B1, V4-B2; shouldFix V4-S1, V4-S2

reviewer: Claude 2, independent, authored none of v2-v5
bindsTo: NOTHING. Independent design-contract review. Does not mark DR-103 SATISFIED, does not mark QUALIFIED, does not edit file 08, does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/.
verdictBasis: 2 blockers, 2 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.

blockers.title: v5 declares that no lock of any form is producible until DR-111, but two test-corpus class members still require lock artifacts with no deferral
detail: v5 states the no-lock rule at three sites and they agree: /lockSchema/fields[resolutionInputs]/semantics ('NO lock is producible until DR-111 closes ... An exact-pin of one or many admitted tuples is a custody copy, not a completed compatible resolution, and is not a lock'); /identityDependencies/dependencies[ID-DEP-4]/consequence ('No lock of any form - exact-pin or constrained, one component or many - is producible until DR-111 closes'); and /testCorpusRequirements/classes[TC-ACCEPT]/requires[5], which defers the TC-ACCEPT lock member.

The repair was applied at the TC-ACCEPT site only. Two other required class members still demand a lock artifact and are byte-identical to v2: TC-SIG/requires[2] = 'artifact bytes vs lock digest mismatch', and TC-BYTE-EXACT/requires[0] = 'a fixture whose admission digest, index custody digest, AND LOCK DIGEST all recompute from stored bytes'.

Neither carries a DR-111 deferral, a conditionalRequires demotion, or any scopeNote. TC-SIG already has a conditionalRequires mechanism (used for ENVELOPE_MISMATCH) and TC-BYTE-EXACT already has a scopeNote (used for canonicalization vectors), so the artifact has two established conventions for exactly this and used neither here.
blockers.whyItMatters: A fixture author reading this contract is required to produce two lock fixtures that the same contract says cannot exist. That is the dispatch's 'any still-producible lock' attack arriving from the requirements side rather than the production side: v5 closed lock PRODUCTION at every site but left lock REQUIREMENTS open at two of three. The corpus cell for DR-103 cannot be discharged against a requirements set that is internally unsatisfiable.
blockers.remedy: Defer TC-SIG/requires[2] and TC-BYTE-EXACT/requires[0]'s lock clause to DR-111 on the pattern already used at TC-ACCEPT/requires[5] - or move them to conditionalRequires/scopeNote as those two classes already do for their other DR-111- and ID-DEP-1-conditional members. TC-BYTE-EXACT's member is separable: its admission-digest and index-custody-digest halves remain producible today and only the lock-digest clause needs deferring.

blockers.title: Codex V4-S2 is marked REPAIRED while the field Codex named is untouched: three binding sources still assert measuredAtAuthoring true, and I measured all three as moved
detail: Codex V4-S2's finding text names the field explicitly: 'corpusHeadAtAuthoring and reMeasurementAtV2 still explicitly describe v2, while bindingSources say measuredAtAuthoring ... Three live whole-document source pins remain moved.' Its required repair: 'record Codex S2 as partially repaired/carried, or SCOPE THE MEASUREMENT FIELDS explicitly to v2 and add v4 authoring custody.'

v5's repair is a single ADD of /sources/reMeasurementAtV5. The measurement fields themselves are byte-identical to v2: all five bindingSources still carry "measuredAtAuthoring": true, including SRC-08, SRC-D and SRC-FRZ. The new note therefore CONTRADICTS the machine-readable field rather than scoping or correcting it - the field says measured-at-authoring, the note says 'not this-authoring claims'.

I re-measured every pin against live bytes. SRC-02 1811c682... and SRC-03 52158469... still match, so v5's re-measurement claim for those two is accurate. The other three have all moved: SRC-08 pinned f0d72536eb1c55e62e43f02ca859a32aa5a8fd096719199d087d8aa665f7b00d, live 1cdcf9d4071a6c5eaa7cd7d28fac288eaced796c9ee906b6f1db0f7a4b1f95b3; SRC-D pinned a3d0d26675bfa0512daebd2f5fcc818346aec7cc1ac2eb07878647ce5e2ddb8f, live 12d192f758f48f692e69cb410a1d7a9bf776c765257c8e910272d3de457ec3e3; SRC-FRZ pinned 93a4f74f744a49e09a8ccc38b8355bdeb85dccc5c99c193eda97659ad8e8e1ab, live e809d4395f394a507c36c23c069d566c838b2283c931b6d2d13797be53406dbd.

v5 writes that those three 'MAY have moved since v2'. They have. v5 measured SRC-02 and SRC-03 at v5 authoring and reported both accurately, so the tooling and the intent were present; the three pins that actually moved were the ones left unmeasured and hedged.
The repairLog entry V4-S2 carries disposition REPAIRED.
blockers.whyItMatters: These are not incidental citations. SRC-08 carries the DR-103 register row this artifact quotes for its own authority claim; SRC-D carries D-002, D-008 and D-012, which the identity, declaration and naming rules rest on; SRC-FRZ carries the section 7.5 sweep that warrants RJ-6/DUPLICATE_JSON_KEY. For a design contract whose whole discipline is exact-byte custody, asserting measuredAtAuthoring on three warrant sources whose bytes no longer exist in the tree is the defect the discipline exists to prevent. It is also the second successive successor to leave this finding unrepaired while recording it as handled.
blockers.remedy: Set measuredAtAuthoring to false (or rename it measuredAtV2Authoring) on SRC-08, SRC-D and SRC-FRZ, re-measure them at v5 authoring and record the live digests alongside the v2 pins with a note on what changed in the cited sections, and change /repairLog[V4-S2] disposition from REPAIRED to PARTIALLY-REPAIRED or CARRIED until the fields are corrected.
blockers.substanceCheck: I verified independently that the CITED substance still holds in the moved files, so this is a custody-accounting defect rather than a warrant failure: the live SRC-08 DR-103 row still reads status OPEN with the same decision and acceptance-evidence text; the live SRC-D still carries D-012 at 'DR-104: component identity, namespace and collision policy'; the live SRC-FRZ section 7.5 is still the duplicate-JSON-key sweep.

shouldFix.title: basedOn.method's entry roster is open-ended, so V4-S1's repair claim is not literally met
shouldFix.detail: Codex V4-S1 found that v4's method sentence named a repairLog entry ('Codex-B2') that did not exist. v5's repairLog claims the repair as 'v5 names only real v5 repairLog finding ids'. The sentence reads: 'Every path the v5 repairLog (entries V4-B1, V4-B2, V4-S1, V4-S2, META-v5, plus any Claude v4 findings folded after that verdict lands) does not name is unchanged from v4.' The five named ids are real and I verified all of them resolve. The trailing clause names an unbounded set of entries that do not exist, so the roster cannot be enumerated and a later edit could add entries that the sentence retroactively covers without being amended. This is milder than v4's defect - it is a forward-looking hedge, not a false assertion - but the completeness claim is the mechanism a reviewer relies on, and it should close.
shouldFix.remedy: Drop the trailing clause. If Claude v4 findings are ever folded, that is a v6 act with its own roster.

shouldFix.title: lockSchema.resolved cannot address a (stableId, version, scope)-keyed index entry, and the forward-looking ordering rule is still stated as (stableId, version)
shouldFix.detail: The v3-to-v4 repair made scope identity-bearing: index entries are keyed per (stableId, version, scope) and shadowedBy was widened to that triple so it addresses a unique entry. lockSchema was not carried along. The resolved tuple is still { stableId, provenance, version, manifestDigest, platformTreeEntryCount, artifactDigests } with no scope, so a lock cannot name which index entry it selected - and under D-012 clause 4 a component may be admitted at both scopes at the same version. v5's ordering sentence still reads 'Ordering rule, when locks become producible: entries sorted by (stableId, version)'. That is a normative statement about future locks that is already inconsistent with the entry key it must join to. Deferring lock production does not repair it, because DR-111 owns version-window semantics, not scope identity.
shouldFix.remedy: Add scope to the resolved tuple and to the ordering rule, or state that the lock's custody join to the index is by (stableId, version) plus the resolution's selected scope recorded in resolutionInputs.

advisories.title: lockSchema.purpose still describes the lock as a producible record with no deferral marker
advisories.detail: purpose reads 'The exact-resolution record for a project/operation: which admitted component releases a resolution selected...' - byte-identical to v2. The no-lock-until-DR-111 rule lives only in resolutionInputs.semantics and ID-DEP-4. A reader entering at lockSchema.purpose sees no signal that production is deferred. One clause would close it.

advisories.title: resolutionInputs.type still offers exact-pin and constrained request forms as live alternatives
advisories.detail: The type string is unchanged from v4: 'request: either exact-pin pairs { stableId, version } ... or constrained pairs { stableId, versionConstraint }'. The semantics field immediately below now says neither is producible. The type is a shape declaration for a future lock, so this is not a contradiction, but the two fields read against each other.

advisories.title: The dual-scope exclusion is not provenance-qualified while the multi-version exclusion is
advisories.detail: collisionUniverse and RJ-2 (both unchanged from v4) exclude 'same-(stableId, provenance) multi-version coexistence AND same-(stableId, version) dual-scope admission'. The second exclusion omits provenance, so a different-provenance claimant at the same (stableId, version) under another scope falls outside RJ-2's cross-entry half. RJ-1 still refuses it - v4 correctly made RJ-1's independence explicit - so there is no hole, but the two exclusions are asymmetric for no stated reason.

advisories.title: collisionUniverse's shadowedBy phrasing is stale
advisories.detail: '...which is also how shadowedBy plus version identifies a unique entry' reads as though shadowedBy were still the (stableId, scope) pair. Since v4, shadowedBy IS the (stableId, version, scope) triple, so 'plus version' is redundant and misdescribes the field.

advisories.title: RJ-2's DIFFERENT-(stableId, provenance) qualifier still attaches to only the last enumerated item
advisories.detail: The trigger enumerates 'the reserved list (unconditional), live names/aliases, live entries' MOUNTED ROOT COMMAND NAMES of a DIFFERENT (stableId, provenance), or within the manifest's own command tree'. The qualifier sits on the third item; 'live names/aliases' is unqualified. The trailing exclusion sentence closes it, so this is drafting only.

attackListDisposition.result: REFUTED at the production sites, CONFIRMED at the requirement sites
attackListDisposition.detail: All three production statements agree that no lock of any cardinality or form is producible until DR-111. But TC-SIG and TC-BYTE-EXACT still require lock fixtures - see V5-B1.

attackListDisposition.attack: Calling a custody copy a lock
attackListDisposition.detail: Stated twice and unambiguously: 'An exact-pin of one or many admitted tuples is a custody copy, not a completed compatible resolution, and is not a lock' (lockSchema) and 'A non-validating custody copy of admitted tuples is not a lock' (ID-DEP-4). TC-ACCEPT's present evidence is redirected to index custody, not to a pin renamed as a lock. This repairs the v4 cardinality contradiction cleanly: v4's lockSchema permitted a plural dependency-free set while ID-DEP-4 said 'the sole presently producible lock is ... a single admitted component'.

collisionUniverse and RJ-2's trigger are byte-identical to v4 and carry the explicit carve-outs: 'RJ-1 is unaffected: it is a SAME-stableId rule by construction and still refuses a different-provenance claimant of a live or retired ID' and 'RJ-1 is not this rule.' RJ-1's own trigger is byte-identical back to v2. The exclusion is provenance-qualified at the multi-version arm, so a different-provenance claimant stays inside RJ-2's cross-entry half as well.
entryShape.stableId still keys entries per (stableId, version, scope) and shadowedBy is still the matching triple; both byte-identical to v4. No regression.

attackListDisposition.attack: Silent v4-to-v5 path outside the v5 repairLog
attackListDisposition.detail: My recursive diff found exactly 21 changed/added/removed paths. Every one is named by a v5 repairLog entry: V4-B1 (lockSchema semantics, TC-ACCEPT requires/5), V4-B2 (ID-DEP-4 consequence, lockSchema semantics), V4-S1 (basedOn/method), V4-S2 (sources/reMeasurementAtV5), META-v5 (artifact, version, basedOn, appliesFindingsOf, reviewGuidance). repairLog[0:27] is byte-identical to v4's complete log, so no landed repair was rewritten. This is a genuine improvement and it holds.

status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING, authorityClaim NONE and all nine whatThisDoesNotDo items are byte-identical to v4. appliesFindingsOf.standing volunteers 'This successor does not SATISFY DR-103 and does not author fixtures.' No creep at any of the 21 diff sites.
